title: Create a folder on a Remote from the directory picker
body:
Let the user create a folder on a Remote from the remote directory picker. The picker (src/remote_browse.rs model + ssh listing, src/remote_browse_ui.rs widget, hosted by src/remote_dir_prompt.rs and the Remotes pane edit form in src/remotes_pane.rs) lists a Remote's folders under the Directory field and is read-only today. The human asked for a way to make folders from it. This reverses the earlier "nothing is created on the Remote" rule for this one explicit action; update the spec and feature doc to say so.
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-remote-sessions-design.md (the directory picker part). Feature doc: docs/remote-sessions.md (gotchas only).
Blocked by: Fix review findings on the remote directory picker
Decided, do not reopen:
- One action: "new folder" inside the directory the list is currently showing. No rename, no delete, no files.
- It is always explicit: the user chooses the action, types a name, and confirms with Enter. Nothing is created by typing a path that does not exist, by opening a Session, or by saving the form.
- One level only (no parents created), and never overwrite: if the name exists, say so. The name is a single path component: reject empty, ".", "..", anything containing a path separator (/ always; \ and : too for Windows shells), control characters, or a leading "-" is allowed only because the command uses "--" (test it).
- Runs over ssh with BatchMode, off the UI thread, with a deadline, built with the existing quoting (sh_quote / ps_quote, posix_line / utf16le_b64) so the name and parent are data, never shell text. Posix: cd -- <parent> then mkdir -- <name>. Pwsh / WindowsPowerShell: New-Item -ItemType Directory with -LiteralPath semantics for the parent, labelled untested like the rest of the Windows path. Failures become plain messages (already exists, permission denied, no such parent, cannot log in without a prompt) that say what to do.
- On success the listing for that parent is refreshed (drop its cache entry), the field is set to the new folder, and the list shows the new (empty) folder, so Enter in the field opens or saves there.
Do:
1. Model and command in src/remote_browse.rs: name validation, the mkdir script for each shell, the ssh argv (same shape as list_args), result parsing with the same sentinel approach the listing uses. Table tests, a test on the argv, and extend the executed-script test (the one that runs the real Posix script with sh against a temp directory) to create a folder with hostile names (it's, $(x), -x, a name with spaces) and to hit already-exists and missing-parent.
2. Widget in src/remote_browse_ui.rs: a "+ new folder" row as the first row of the list (after ".."), reachable by mouse and by a key shown in the hint (for example N while the list is focused; it must not steal N while the text field is focused). Choosing it turns that row into an inline name field in the same row slot: Enter creates, Esc cancels back to the list, the list height does not change. While creating, show progress in words; on failure show the message on the breadcrumb/status line in the danger colour and keep the typed name for another try.
3. Both hosts (directory prompt and Remotes form) get it through the shared widget. Every hint still fits one line (PANE_MIN_W in the form), and the first-Esc-returns-to-field rule still holds: Esc in the name field goes back to the list, not out of the prompt.
Design bar (a designer reviews this from the code afterwards): theme tokens only; the "+ new folder" row reads as an action, not a folder (not colour alone); the name field and the Directory field can never both look focused; Enter never does two things in one state (create vs descend vs open); nothing shifts when the result arrives; copy names the Remote and the parent folder ("New folder in ~/Projects on falador").
The test Remote is andy@192.168.8.168 (also reachable as andy@100.102.251.37; key login, never ask for a password). You may create and then remove throwaway folders ONLY under /tmp/foreman-mkdir-test on it to check the Posix command by hand, and must remove that directory afterwards. Touch nothing else there.
Done when:
- the tests above pass, plus egui::Context::run tests: N opens the name field only when the list is focused; Enter creates once (key repeat does not create twice); Esc returns to the list; list height unchanged across idle / naming / creating / failed
- a created folder appears in the refreshed listing and the field holds its path
- the full test suite passes
- the final report lists the states the human should capture with build-screenshot and what was run against the test Remote
Gate: cargo test --target-dir target/agent
